question: The Jhelum River rises from which of the following sources?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Spring at Verinag**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Jhelum River **originates from the **Verinag spring **situated in the **Kashmir Valley**, nestled at the base of the **Pir Panjal range in Anantnag.**
 
• It traverses through **Srinagar and Wular Lake** before exiting into Pakistan via a narrow gorge.
 
• As the westernmost of the five rivers in the** Punjab region, **the Jhelum spans a length of 725 kilometers.
 
• Functioning as a tributary of the Chenab River, the Jhelum flows across the Indian-administered territory of Jammu and Kashmir, subsequently entering Pakistani-administered Kashmir, and eventually reaching the Pakistani province of Punjab.
 
• Its course meanders northwestward from the northern slopes of the Pir Panjal Range, traversing the scenic Vale of Kashmir until it reaches Wular Lake in Srinagar, where its flow is regulated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Verinag Spring, **situated in Anantnag, Jammu and Kashmir, India, is renowned for its deep blue water, sourced from the base of a mountain spur.
 
• The Brahmaputra River originates from the **Chemayungdung glacier** within the Kailash range near Lake Mansarovar.
 
• **Lake Mansarovar, **located in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, holds the distinction of being the highest freshwater lake globally, with an elevation of 14,950 meters.
 
• **Lake Rakshastal,** alternatively known as Rakshas Tal, is a saltwater lake located in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
